title: Adaptive Holdoff Horizon for Continuous Batcher to Prevent KV-starvation
author: Evelyn Park
description: Motivation: KV-heavy workloads experience intermittent starvation when continuous batching aggressively prefers large coalesced batches; long-lived KV pins and infrequent small requests can get delayed, increasing P99 latency and producing client retries. This PR implements an adaptive "holdoff horizon" for the continuous batcher that reduces starvation by temporarily lowering coalescing aggressiveness for queues showing age or KV-pin pressure. The change adds a lightweight horizon heuristic plus a decay-driven holdoff credit that is allocated per-queue and rebalanced periodically. Key design points: 1) Holdoff Horizon: a configurable time horizon that tells the batcher to limit waiting for additional inflight tokens beyond the horizon for aged queues. 2) Adaptive credits: queues earn holdoff credits when they see repeated long wait times or failed KV-pin probes; credits decay exponentially to avoid permanent priority inversion. 3) Backoff compatibility: integrates with existing soft reservations and ticket leases to ensure we do not starve throughput for throughput-sensitive routes. 4) Deterministic test harness and perf microbench included. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated pools -> gradual rollout to hosted API with feature flag and 10% traffic ramp -> full rollout after 2 days of metrics stability. This PR includes implementation, tests, perf harness, docs, and a console dashboard snippet for the new metrics. Checklist: - [x] Core algorithm and API - [x] Unit tests for correctness and deterministic scheduler scenarios - [x] Perf harness and regression tests - [x] Telemetry emitting holdoff_credit, horizon_hits, kv_pin_failures - [x] Docs and rollout plan - [x] Feature flag gating and canary config

ci_checks: lint: fail (style on holdoff_horizon.h) -> fixed in e4f7aa2 -> pass
benchmark_results: KV-heavy closed-loop (tail-heavy mix) before: P50=45ms P95=190ms P99=360ms; after: P50=43ms P95=120ms P99=220ms
Mixed short/long seqs throughput: unchanged within noise (±1.5%) across 1M requests/sec emulation
KV pin timeouts observed: reduced by 88% on targeted queues in canary cluster
Token cost per successful request: ~6% reduction due to fewer retries and fewer long-wait backoffs
CPU overhead: +0.4% on scheduler hot path in worst-case synthetic; deemed acceptable
release_notes: Introduce adaptive holdoff horizon for the continuous batcher to mitigate KV-pin starvation on mixed workloads. Improves P99 in KV-heavy scenarios and reduces retries. Feature gated behind 'batcher.holdoff.enabled'; default off for hosted. See docs/operations/batcher-holdoff.md for tuning guidance.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover decay scheduling, horizon edge cases, and interaction with soft reservations. Perf harness scripts included under tests/perf; run with TEST_SCENARIO=kv_starvation_mixed. Canary for 10% traffic, promote after 48h stability checks on P99 and kv_pin_failures.
rollout_plan: Canary on dedicated pools (feature flag true) -> 10% hosted API traffic for 24-48h -> monitor holdoff.horizon_hits and kv_pin_failures; rollback if P99 increases or cpu overhead >2% -> full rollout after 48h stable
notes_for_ops: If you see horizon_hits spiking with no improvement to P99, reduce holdoff.horizon_ms by 25% for the problematic route and open ENG-2381. Telemetry keys: holdoff.credit, holdoff.horizon_hits, holdoff.kv_pin_failures. Dashboard tile included in docs.
